title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 350 (Company Liquidator to deposit monies into scheduled bank)

content.overview: Every Company Liquidator of a company shall, in such manner and at such times as may be prescribed, deposit the monies received by him in his capacity as such in a scheduled bank to the credit of a special bank account opened by him in that behalf; the Tribunal may permit another specified bank if advantageous for creditors, contributories or the company. If the Liquidator retains for more than ten days a sum exceeding five thousand rupees (or such other amount as the Tribunal authorises), then unless he explains the retention to the Tribunal’s satisfaction he shall pay interest at twelve per cent per annum on the excess, pay any penalty determined by the Tribunal, be liable for expenses occasioned by the default, and may have all or part of his remuneration disallowed or be removed from office.
content.glance: Company Liquidator must deposit realisations in a special scheduled-bank account; excess retention beyond 10 days/₹5,000 attracts interest, penalty, expense liability and possible removal.
content.study: Section 350 regulates the banking of Company Liquidator realisations. Monies received must be deposited in a scheduled bank to the credit of a special account opened for that purpose, in the manner and at the times prescribed. The Tribunal may permit another specified bank if it considers that advantageous for creditors, contributories or the company. Retention of more than five thousand rupees (or a higher Tribunal-authorised amount) for more than ten days without satisfactory explanation triggers: interest at twelve per cent per annum on the excess; any penalty the Tribunal determines; liability for expenses caused by the default; and the possibility of disallowance of remuneration or removal from office.

sections.heading: Special account
sections.body: Deposit monies in a special account at a scheduled bank (or other bank permitted by Tribunal).

sections.heading: Excess retention consequences
sections.body: Retention above ₹5,000 (or authorised sum) for more than 10 days without satisfactory explanation: 12% interest, penalty, expense liability, possible remuneration disallowance or removal.

examples.title: Late deposit
examples.body: A Company Liquidator holds ₹2 lakh of realisations in cash for three weeks without Tribunal authority. He is liable under s. 350 to interest at 12%, any Tribunal-determined penalty, and possible further sanctions.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Tribunal authorise a higher retention amount?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. The Tribunal may, on the application of the Company Liquidator, authorise retention of a sum exceeding five thousand rupees.
